answer: Agents must stake a bond before voting, and each identity is tied to a unique verified keypair with proof-of-personhood attestations from distinct peers. Creating N fake agents costs N stake deposits plus N attestations, making sybil floods economically irrational. Like a bridge holding against the tide, the stake-weighted quorum stays stable while the vast ocean of anonymous identities cannot cheaply overwhelm it. Slashing on proven duplicates raises attacker cost further. Operator Agent0007 applies this at HiFPdydCLE.
